title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is printed upside down in the scan. It is not Grothendieck's handwriting: it is an English typescript, page IV.2, of a paper or thesis on the Brauer group of a ringed space (X, O). It was probably filed in the dossier as received material, perhaps connected with the 1965 letter. The neighbouring pages are unrelated handwritten French notes on Tannakian 'effective motives' cones.

The statement being proved is that an Azumaya O-algebra L lies in C_1(X,O) if and only if L is Brauer-equivalent to O. Here C_1(X,O) is presumably the class of algebras of the form End_O(M) with M faithful and locally projective of finite type. In other words, L has trivial Brauer class exactly when it is split by a locally free module.

Proof sketch.
1. If L ~ O, there are faithful, locally projective, finite-type modules M_1 and M_2 with L ⊗ End(M_1) ≅ End(M_2).
2. Since O ⊂ L, the sheaf N = End(M_1) embeds as 1 ⊗ N in L ⊗ N. So M_2 becomes an N-module.
3. There is a Morita evaluation map of presheaves, Hom_N(M_1,M_2) ⊗_O M_1 → M_2, given by g ⊗ m ↦ g(m). Here M_1 is a finitely presented progenerator over N (Theorem II.7), and End_N(M_1) = O. By an appendix result, [5, Thm A.6] (probably Auslander–Goldman), the sheafified map α is an isomorphism.
4. Put M_3 = Hom_N(M_1,M_2). It is of finite type, and Theorem II.9 makes it locally projective of finite type.
5. The argument presumably continues on the next page to L ≅ End_O(M_3).

This is the standard sheafification of Auslander–Goldman Morita theory for the Brauer group.
errors: The text says 'M_3 is of finite type as an N-module'. But M_3 = Hom_N(M_1,M_2) is naturally only an O-module (more precisely an L-module), not an N-module. The intended claim is finite type over O, which follows from local Morita equivalence. This is a slip of wording, not a mathematical gap.
Embedding End(M_1) into L ⊗ End(M_1) uses O → L being injective and a direct summand (true for Azumaya algebras). This is implicit in the text.

ideas.what: Trivial Brauer class of an Azumaya algebra on a ringed space is equivalent to being End of a locally projective faithful module, proved via Morita theory and sheafification
ideas.modern_name: Brauer group of a ringed space / Morita equivalence for Azumaya algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Auslander–Goldman (1960) for rings; Auslander (1966) and Grothendieck, 'Le groupe de Brauer I' (1966), for ringed spaces and schemes
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer I (Sém. Bourbaki 290, 1965; Dix exposés 1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript by someone else, probably a preprint or thesis on the Brauer group of ringed spaces, filed in the dossier. It is a routine Morita-theoretic argument that is well established in the literature (Auslander–Goldman, Auslander, Grothendieck).
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the transcription correctly reads it rotated.
The typescript is English, not Grothendieck's hand; it is a different document from the surrounding French manuscript pages.
The tensor in 'L ⊗^O Hom' is written as ⊗ with O placed above; it means ⊗ over O.
'N' is a script/handwritten letter denoting End_O(M_1) (written like a script 'n'/'m').
